messages:
sam (support): FYI customer ryan reporting a sharp drop in vectors/sec starting ~02:00 UTC. tokens/sec unchanged. ryan says embeddings latency spiked and 429s briefly showed up. attaching their repro steps below.
ryan (acct): repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood/infer/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{\"inputs\":[...2000 short texts...]}' -- we get normal token counts but vectors/sec is ~25% of previous.
lee (eng-runtime): thanks. can you paste the exact response headers and any 429/401 bodies? also which model variant/size?
ryan (acct): model: open-embed-16k-v2. headers: x-request-id: req_9f3, x-infer-latency-ms: 1220, x-tokens-out: 1984, x-vectors-out: 1984. no 500s, a few 429s earlier, body for 429: '{\"error\":\"rate_limited\"}'.
sam (support): we saw similar token-vs-vector mismatches before when batching or sidecar changes rolled. marking eng-runtime and eng-ml.
anya (sre): I pulled infra metrics around req_9f3: gpu_queue_len spiked to 140 on pod sidecar-3, GPU util stayed ~45% but p99 latency hopped. queue depth suggests lots of tiny batches piling up.
mike (eng-ml): interesting: if sidecar batching got disabled, many single-request batches would increase per-request overhead and reduce vectors/sec throughput even with tokens stable. can you check BATCH_WINDOW_MS and MAX_BATCH_SIZE in sidecar config?
lee (eng-runtime): checked config on the node that hosted customer traffic: BATCH_WINDOW_MS=2, MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 — both look fine. but I see an autoscaler rollout to sidecar image v1.3.7 at 01:58 — that image has a batching change (we thought safe).
anya (sre): correlate logs: sidecar v1.3.7 emitted repeated auth-refresh calls for that API key: "refresh_token: expired_token" every ~120s which blocked its request-processing goroutine briefly (10-50ms) during token refresh. multiplied by many clients this becomes noticeable.
lee (eng-runtime): if token refresh is blocking batching thread, that would fragment batches. can we repro locally with a short harness?
mike (eng-ml): repro steps I ran: 
```
# sim harness
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://local-sidecar/emb -H "X-Api-Key: expired" -d '{"inputs":["text"]}' &
done
wait
```
with sidecar v1.3.6: vectors/sec ~1200; with 1.3.7 + simulated refresh latency (sleep 30ms) vectors/sec ~420.
sam (support): oof. so two issues: 1) sidecar rollout introduced blocking refresh behavior, 2) autoscaler concentrated traffic to nodes with sidecar v1.3.7 so GPU queue depth increased but utilization stayed moderate.
lee (eng-runtime): mitigation proposals: rollback sidecar rollout on affected cluster (canary partial rollback), patch to make refresh non-blocking (v1.3.8), and add circuit-breaker on auth path to fail fast and not stall batching thread.
anya (sre): immediate hotfix: scale up sidecar replicas on the nodepool to spread incoming requests (kubectl scale deploy sidecar --replicas=6) and add a temporary routing rule to shift some traffic to older pool. I'll run that now.
sam (support): ryan — we'll do a partial rollback / traffic shift and monitor vectors/sec. ETA ~15m. sorry for the disruption. :sorry: :heart:
ryan (acct): thanks. updating my team. appreciate the quick triage.
lee (eng-runtime): also adding long-term observability: emit batch_size_histogram, per-sidecar auth-refresh-latency, and pipeline fragment metric (fraction of single-item batches). will open tickets.
mike (eng-ml): notes for postmortem: root cause = sidecar auth-refresh blocking I/O introduced in v1.3.7 + rollout concentration => batching fragmentation => GPU queue depth spike => vectors/sec regression while tokens/sec stayed similar.
anya (sre): monitoring alert runbook: if vectors/sec drops >30% and gpu_queue_len > 100 with gpu_util < 70% -> route traffic away from latest sidecar image and alert eng-runtime.
sam (support): leaving repro artifacts and my test curl payload in the thread. closing loop after rollback verified.
ops-bot: deploy rollback to sidecar v1.3.6 started by anya at 1777000300, status: in_progress
anya (sre): rollback finished at 1777000365, vectors/sec recovered to baseline within 90s, gpu_queue_len dropped below 20.
sam (support): thanks team — will follow up with a short incident summary and customer note.
lee (eng-runtime): created PR with non-blocking refresh patch and added integration test simulating high auth-latency.
mike (eng-ml): add to model ops playbook: consider varying batch window when sidecar auth latency detected to avoid fragmentation.
ryan (acct): confirmed recovery on our side. thanks all.
